name: Chicken Yassa
summary: Chicken marinated in lemon, mustard and a mountain of onions, grilled then simmered into a sharp, sweet sauce.
story: Yassa comes from the Casamance region in southern Senegal and is now eaten across the country and in neighbouring Gambia. It is a popular dish for family meals and gatherings, served over white rice.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, pepper, salt, oil and half the sliced onions. Add the chicken and coat well. Marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.

steps.title: Grill the chicken
steps.text: Lift the chicken out, keeping the marinade and onions. Grill or broil for 8-10 minutes per side until deeply browned and lightly charred. It does not need to cook through.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: Heat a little oil in a heavy pot and add the remaining onions with the marinated onions. Cook on medium-low for 15-20 minutes, stirring, until completely soft, golden and sweet.

steps.title: Add the sauce liquid
steps.text: Pour in the leftover marinade, stock cube, carrot and water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, then add the whole scotch bonnet.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Nestle the grilled chicken in the onions, cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes until the meat is tender and pulls from the bone and the sauce is thick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the olives and taste. It should be sharp, sweet and peppery; add a squeeze of lemon if flat and more salt if needed. Remove the pepper before serving.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon over steaming white rice with plenty of the onion sauce.

tips: Do not rush the onions; slow cooking makes the sauce sweet and silky.
Marinate long enough for the lemon to soften the meat.
Keep the scotch bonnet whole for flavour without overwhelming heat.
Grilling first adds a smoky depth that is the signature of good yassa.

swaps.swap: Traditional recipes use Senegalese mustard; Dijon is the closest match.
Use fish such as tilapia (yassa poisson); reduce simmering time to 10 minutes.
